claims: Artemis II lunar flyby live coverage starts at 1 p.m. EDT on April 6, 2026, via NASA+, the NASA YouTube channel, and NASA's social media.
Coverage includes live views of the Moon from the Orion spacecraft on Netflix, Apple TV, Hulu, and Amazon Prime.
NASA+ and YouTube provide continuous, comprehensive coverage starting at 1 p.m. EDT on April 6, 2026.
Netflix, Peacock, and other major platforms will host the NASA feed.
The Artemis Real-Time Orbit Website (AROW) is the official NASA tracker to monitor the spacecraft's position, speed, and distance.
AROW is available on desktop and as a mobile app.
On April 6, 2026, at 1:56 p.m. EDT, the Artemis II crew breaks the distance record for humans from Earth.
On April 6, 2026, at 2:45 p.m. EDT, the lunar flyby observation period begins.
On April 6, 2026, at 6:44 p.m. EDT, communications loss is expected for approximately 40 minutes as Orion goes behind the moon.
On April 6, 2026, at 7:02 p.m. EDT, closest approach to the Moon occurs.
The NASA app provides augmented reality views of the mission.
